title: Non-resident compounding pharmacy licences and the non-resident pharmacy's duty to comply with Massachusetts pharmacy law
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 6.02(5), a pharmacy located outside of Massachusetts may not dispense or ship any sterile compounded preparation into Massachusetts unless it holds a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license and a non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy license, and under 247 CMR 6.02(6) it may not dispense or ship any complex non-sterile compounded preparation into Massachusetts unless it holds a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license and a non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy license. 247 CMR 6.09 sets out the applications for non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy, non-resident sterile compounding pharmacy and non-resident complex non-sterile compounding pharmacy licenses. Under 247 CMR 9.20, a non-resident pharmacy shall comply with all Massachusetts laws and regulations governing the practice of pharmacy when filling, dispensing, or shipping medications into Massachusetts, unless otherwise specified.
exam_relevance: Tests the licences a pharmacy outside Massachusetts needs before shipping sterile or complex non-sterile compounded preparations into Massachusetts, and its duty to comply with Massachusetts pharmacy law when it does.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations
Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

common_confusions: A pharmacy outside Massachusetts shipping sterile or complex non-sterile compounded preparations into Massachusetts needs both a non-resident Drug Store Pharmacy license and the matching non-resident compounding pharmacy license.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's publications of 247 CMR 6.00 (PDF, Mass. Register #1546, 4/25/2025) and 247 CMR 9.00 (PDF, Mass. Register #1536, 12/6/2024) on mass.gov.
